questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I am studying Japanese Studies and exchange was a crucial part of my bachelor's degree. I wanted to dive into the language and culture of the field I was studying, so for this reason going to a Japanese University seemed obvious. Ristumeikan University was attractive due to its profile as internationally oriented and its location in the cultural hub of Kyoto.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Ritsumeikan University takes very good care of its exchange students and furthermore, I was helped out by people at my dormitory.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was assisted by Resident Managers at my dorm in opening a bank account, signing up for Japanese insurance etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I highly recommend International House Utano. It is a smaller dorm, that is relatively far from campus but well-connected with buses. I have only good things to say about that place.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I think the most important thing to consider is what aspects are important to the individual. Some people will prioritize living closer to the campus, some people value having access to a private bathroom etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The course registration process took place online. There were course descriptions available that where very easy to comprehend.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I was guided by Resident Managers at my dorm.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was in a way over-successful. The university had warned the students that it was not likely that all of our priorities would be met, so I signed up for more classes than I needed. In the end, this turned out to be a mistake on my part as I was granted a spot in all the classes I wanted and needed.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to create a schedule that is not too intense and maybe I would not recommend more than three different classes in a day.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was mostly satisfied, but a certain course, International Migration, was highly criticizable. The professor never seemed prepared for classes and struggled with structure and communication.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: In my experience, the Japanese language courses had a very appropriate level, while my additional courses were rather easy and sometimes slightly superficial.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching at Ritsumeikan University is much more focused on attendance, writing assignments and making presentations than what I am used to from the University of Copenhagen. However, I never felt that much was expected from us in class discussions, and sometimes I found that the teachings were slightly superficial.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I highly recommend the course Cross-cultural Studies. It allowed me to discuss topics with Japanese students and make many good friends.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: In general, most things are cheaper compared to Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are lots of clubs and activities available for everyone.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All sorts of clubs and gatherings. Sports, culture, music etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not have much time to participate in club activities due to the large amount of credits required by the University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Kyoto offers lots of beautiful temples and shrines. I also recommend people try traditional Japanese sweets, wagashi, which Kyoto is famous for. There are also many amazing hiking routes close to the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was surprisingly easy. I was very grateful to the community of the dorm for making the transition simple.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Take courses that are open to both Japanese and foreign students. And use BBP (Beyond Borders Plaza), which is an open space for people to socialize.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Initially, I struggled a bit with the levels of formality that are connected to the Japanese language.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I absolutely adore the city of Kyoto. It has an amazing atmosphere, cuisine and surroundings.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Get out of your comfort zone, explore the city as much as possible and remember to take time off on the weekends to recharge. Exchange can be very overwhelming.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are a student of Japanese Studies like myself, I would advise you to put most of your energy into the language classes provided at Ritsumeikan University. The University of Copenhagen requires students to take quite a lot of courses and it is difficult to give it your all in all of them.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange is how drastically my language abilities have improved.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The biggest challenge for me was time. I needed to dedicate so much time to my additional courses that it was hard to find the time for socializing and enjoying the surroundings to the fullest.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No other comments.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
